title: Scheduled evidence exports and dashboard delivery for compliance (PDF/CSV + residency-aware delivery)
creator: Asha Verma
description:
Summary: Build first-class automated compliance reporting that can produce scheduled PDF and CSV evidence bundles and deliver them to residency-appropriate endpoints (S3 in region, secure FTP, or email with encrypted attachments). This feature surfaces on the Compliance dashboard and supports tenant-level retention settings, per-tenant data residency constraints, and audit traceability (signed export hashes and delivery receipts).

Why: Customers in regulated industries require regular, human-readable evidence of data handling and retention policies for audits. Currently they manually stitch logs, retention snapshots, and console screenshots. A native scheduled export + delivery system reduces manual effort, lowers time-to-evidence, and helps close renewal conversations with enterprise customers requiring demonstrable residency and retention controls.

Scope (MVP):
- UI in Console Compliance section to configure scheduled exports (daily/weekly/monthly), format (PDF summary, CSV raw data), recipient endpoint (regional S3 bucket, SFTP, secure email), and retention snapshot window.
- Export content templates: Audit summary (PDF), Raw records (CSV) with optional PII redaction rules, Retention snapshot (CSV) showing per-tenant retention policy enforcement over the period.
- Residency-aware delivery: exports for EU customers stored/delivered from EU region only; US customers from US region only.
- Evidence bundles must include a generated SHA-256 manifest and a signed delivery receipt logged to the audit trail.
- Scheduled job runner with retry/backoff, alerting to customer and Redwood support when delivery fails repeatedly.

Out of scope (MVP): ad-hoc one-off exports via API (will be follow-up), export of full request/response token streams (privacy review required), native long-term archival service (customers can deliver to their own buckets).
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: Users can create a scheduled export policy with cadence, format (PDF/CSV), recipients, and regional constraint; saved policy persists and is editable.
Export generation: System can generate a PDF audit summary and compressed CSV payload for a sample EU tenant and US tenant within the configured cadence.

Residency enforcement: For an EU tenant configured with EU-only delivery, generated files are stored and delivered only from EU-hosted infrastructure (test proof: file metadata shows eu-west-1 storage and delivery endpoint).
Integrity evidence: Each export bundle includes a SHA-256 manifest and a signed delivery receipt recorded in the tenant audit log with timestamps and delivery status.

Delivery channels: Exports can be delivered to S3 (region-specific), SFTP, and as encrypted email attachments using customer-provided public key; failures trigger an alert to the support queue and an automated retry policy (3 attempts with exponential backoff).
Retention snapshot: CSV shows applied retention rules and the list of records deleted or marked for deletion during the snapshot window for the tenant; matches system retention enforcement logs.
Performance: Generating and packaging an export for a 30M token tenant should complete within 20 minutes in Dedicated environment (benchmarked during engineering spike).
notes: Design decision: PDF should use a templating engine (HTML-to-PDF) to allow branding and readable audit summaries; engineering prefers wkhtmltopdf or headless Chromium but flagged for infra cost review.
Tradeoff: Including raw token-level data in CSV increases sensitivity and storage; MVP will include pseudonymization toggles and a customer opt-in for token-level exports.
Compliance nuance: Some customers require that the signing key for delivery receipts be customer-managed; plan to add KMS/HSM integration in follow-up (Private deployments first).
Related docs: Confluence spec - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Scheduled+Exports (draft), Security review checklist PR - https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/pull/214
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize API schema for ExportPolicy and ExportRun; finalize PDF/CSV templates with Design.
Week 2: Build scheduled job runner service and residency-aware storage plumbing; implement S3/SFTP/email delivery adapters.
Week 3: Produce audit manifest signing and delivery receipt flow; integrate with audit log and support alerting.
Week 4: Console UI for policy creation/editing, QA, security review, and limited alpha with 3 pilot customers.
Rollout: Alpha -> Beta (2 customers) -> general availability in console-2026.04; Dedicated customers will receive region-specific config knobs in a patch release.
risks: Residency enforcement complexity: ensuring exports are generated and egressed only from approved regions requires infra changes and legal verification.
PII leakage: CSV exports may unintentionally include sensitive tokens; must enforce redaction/pseudonymization policies and require customer acceptance for high-sensitivity exports.
Delivery failures: customers expect SLA for evidence delivery; need clear retry/backoff and escalation procedures to prevent missed audits.
Cost and performance: generating PDFs for very large tenants could impact runtime capacity; may require limiting historical window or parallelizing export generation.
customer_communication: Email template for pilot customers describing feature, expected deliverables, and opt-in steps (to be prepared by PM/Customer Success).
Support runbook for failed deliveries with playbook steps and contact points (Support + Oncall + ENG).
metrics: Number of scheduled export policies created per tenant (weekly)
Export success rate (per-cadence) and mean time to delivery
Time to generate export (P50/P95) for 1M, 10M, 30M token tenants
Number of export-related support tickets after GA
